chunks.text:
data: {"type":"tool","id":"tool-1","name":"ask_pigeon"}

data: {"type":"text","delta":"We are turning to the Stakeholder pigeon to hear how this annual disruption feels from its perspective and what it demands from our shared urban space."}
data: {"type":"artifact_delta","id":"pigeon-1","delta":"None of your papers record exactly what fireworks do to my species. But they show these explosives damage"}
data: {"type":"artifact_delta","id":"pigeon-1","delta":" public health through pollution, trauma, and injuries [1]. In those medical cases, the damage mostly means burns and broken"}
data: {"type":"artifact_delta","id":"pigeon-1","delta":" limbs [2]. I refuse to risk my own bones and lungs for your loud celebrations. Why should we pay the price"}
data: {"type":"text","delta":"The conflict here lies between a deeply rooted human tradition of celebration and the basic physical safety of the animals that"}
data: {"type":"text","delta":" share our squares and roofs. For city planners and residents, this raises the question of whether a brief moment of public entertainment"}
data: {"type":"text","delta":" is worth the physical danger and distress it inflicts on non-human neighbors. \n\nWhat alternatives could Rotterdam use to"}
data: {"type":"text","delta":" mark celebrations without endangering the wildlife that lives here?"}
